channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Nunes Marques assume a presidência do TSE; veja perfis dos ministros da corte
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques assumes the presidency of the TSE in 2026, with André Mendonça as vice-president, marking the first time two ministers appointed by Jair Bolsonaro to the STF simultaneously lead the electoral court. The tribunal will face challenges including the implementation of changes to the Clean Record Law and oversight of AI-generated content, while continuing its role in organizing and supervising elections, reviewing party and candidate financial reports, and adjudicating electoral disputes.

item.title: Lula diz que pediu a Trump entrega de criminosos do Brasil que estão em Miami
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated he requested Donald Trump, during a meeting at the White House, to extradite Brazilian criminals residing in Miami. The remark was made during the launch of the Brazil Against Organized Crime program, which allocates R$ 11 billion to public security.

item.title: Motta defende aplicação da Lei da Dosimetria e crê em decisão favorável do STF
item.description: Hugo Motta, president of the Chamber of Deputies, stated that Congress will oppose the suspension of the Dosimetry Law, approved in 2025, which allows sentence reductions for those involved in the January 8 attacks, including Jair Bolsonaro. He advocates for the STF to uphold the law’s applicability, already approved by a large congressional majority and with the presidential veto overturned. Motta expects the STF plenary to rule in favor of the law.

item.title: Movimentos articulam nome de promotora negra para o STF em encontro com Boulos
item.description: Social movements such as Instituto Juristas Negras and Mulheres Negras Decidem held a closed meeting with the Minister of the General Secretariat of the Presidency, Guilherme Boulos, to advocate for the nomination of a Black female prosecutor to the Supreme Federal Court (STF). The goal is to increase Black and female representation on Brazil’s highest court amid growing pressure for judicial diversity. The initiative reflects political and social mobilizations surrounding the upcoming STF vacancy.

item.title: As duas pesquisas de intenção de voto para presidente nesta semana
item.description: Two presidential voting intention polls will be released this week: Quaest on Wednesday (13) and Datafolha on Friday (15). Both show a tight race between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), with Lula leading in the first round and a technical tie in the second round based on previous surveys. Each poll will include 2,004 interviews with a two-point margin of error.

item.title: Governo deve lançar hoje plano de combate ao crime organizado
item.description: The federal government will launch today a plan to combat organized crime with an estimated investment of R$ 11 billion, focusing on financial strangulation, prison reinforcement, increased homicide clearance rates, and confrontation with arms trafficking. Implementation depends on voluntary adherence by state governments, which will gain access to funds if they adopt the proposals. The event will take place at the Palácio do Planalto with President Lula in attendance.

item.title: Petrobras vende gasolina mais barata e preocupa mercado após balanço do 1° tri
item.description: Petrobras sold gasoline below import parity price in Q1 2026, with a discount ranging from R$0.60 to R$1.20, leading to a 7.2% drop in adjusted net profit to R$32.6 billion. Analysts suggest the pricing policy reflects political interference to curb inflation and shield President Lula’s popularity, despite market dissatisfaction over reduced dividends.

item.title: Governo demorou a adotar plano de combate ao crime organizado por boicote de governadores da oposição, acusam governistas
item.description: Government allies accuse opposition governors of boycotting the Public Security PEC and the Anti-Faction Bill, delaying measures against organized crime. They claim the Lula administration could have implemented integrated federal-state actions since last year, but the articulation of governors from São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Goiás, and Santa Catarina in Congress blocked progress. While acknowledging internal divisions in Lula’s team, allies place primary blame on the opposition, particularly Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, for allegedly aligning with opponents to weaken Lula politically ahead of the 2026 presidential campaign.

item.title: Charge do JCaesar: 12 de maio
item.description: The decision by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to suspend the effects of the Dosimetry Law has triggered a new escalation in the political crisis between the opposition and the Judiciary, reigniting right-wing movements to launch an offensive against the Court. Columnist JCaesar also notes Ciro Gomes' pre-candidacy for the government of Ceará and an explosion in São Paulo's west zone that left one dead and three injured as key highlights in the VEJA roundup.

item.title: Lula sanciona, com vetos, punição mais severa a quem mata policiais
item.description: President Lula signed into law, with vetoes, a bill establishing a stricter disciplinary regime for those who kill police or military personnel on duty. He vetoed sections 3 and 4 for turning an exceptional regime into a rule and ignoring individualized sentencing, and also vetoed the ban on regime progression and conditional release for pre-trial and convicted detainees, citing unconstitutionality and conflict with public interest.

item.title: Aliados de Motta veem poucas chances para PEC da anistia antes da eleição
item.description: Allies of House Speaker Hugo Motta say the opposition’s effort to pass an Amnesty PEC before the 2026 elections has little chance of success, due to lack of political support and isolation of the initiative. Expectations are that the STF will uphold the Dosimetry Law, further weakening the opposition’s push. Even after the elections, the PEC would struggle to secure the 308 votes needed in the Chamber and 49 in the Senate.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Datafolha divulga pesquisa de intenção de voto à Presidência nesta sexta-feira
item.description: Datafolha releases a presidential voting intention poll this Friday, conducted from May 12 to 14 with 2,004 respondents. The survey, registered with TSE under BR-00290/2026, updates April data showing Lula leading with 39%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 35%, Ronaldo Caiado at 5%, and other candidates with lower support.

item.title: Operação da PF mobiliza nova Força Integrada contra o crime organizado e cumpre mais de 230 mandados em 16 estados
item.description: The Federal Police mobilizes the Integrated Force to Combat Organized Crime (FICCO) across 16 states, executing over 230 warrants for arrests and searches in operations targeting drug and arms trafficking, money laundering, and criminal factions. The action is part of the federal government’s new 'Brazil against Organized Crime' program, with R$11 billion in investments announced by President Lula. Notable operations include Paper Stone and Rota Andina in Minas Gerais, Cerco Integrado in Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina, and actions in Paraíba and Paraná.

item.title: Lula improvisa plano de segurança de R$ 11 bilhões para reeleição
item.description: Lula announced an R$11 billion plan to combat organized crime, 20 weeks before the elections, but without agreements with governors or Congress, revealing an improvised move to place public safety on the electoral agenda. The plan marks a shift in his stance, acknowledging federal responsibility for the security crisis after years of blaming state governments. Despite the investment, Lula’s rejection remains high, near 50%, according to recent polls.

item.title: “Joesley está jogando um jogo perigoso pra c…”, diz ex-assessor de Trump
item.description: Jason Miller, former advisor to Donald Trump, accused businessman Joesley Batista of J&F of playing a dangerous game by mediating contact between the U.S. president and Brazil's President Lula. He warned that 'the pendulum always swings back and never forgets,' implying potential political backlash.

item.title: Pesquisa mostra a disputa pela presidência entre os eleitores do Mato Grosso do Sul; veja os números
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading the presidential race in Mato Grosso do Sul with 43% voter intention in both first-round scenarios tested, followed by Lula (PT) at 30% and 29%. Ciro Gomes (PSDB) registers 2% only in the scenario that includes him, despite having ruled out a presidential bid. In the simulated runoff, Bolsonaro expands his lead to 17 points, reaching 51% against Lula’s 34%.

item.title: Coluna da Tribuna: Rodolfo precisa controlar equipe
item.description: The mayor of Apucarana, Rodolfo Mota (União Brasil), categorically denied any division within his administration regarding unrestricted support for Ratinho Junior's gubernatorial candidacy. He emphasized that the alliance remains united and focused on the electoral campaign.

item.title: Neymar na pré-lista da Copa: maioria dos brasileiros quer jogador no Mundial, aponta Datafolha
item.description: A majority of Brazilians (53%) support Neymar's inclusion in Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad, according to a Datafolha poll released in April. Support has increased since June 2025 (from 48%), while opposition decreased from 41% to 34%. Neymar remains on the CBF's preliminary list and awaits the final selection by Carlo Ancelotti, set for April 18, despite ongoing concerns about his physical condition following recent injuries.

item.title: Lula deve priorizar Redata para evitar perder investimentos, diz deputado
item.description: Deputy Julio Lopes (PP-RJ) urges the Lula government to prioritize the approval of Redata, a bill granting federal tax exemptions for data center equipment, warning that delays risk losing investments to competitors like Argentina, which has allegedly attracted over US$100 billion. He cautions that congressional postponement could push the vote beyond the 2026 elections, while industry leaders, backed by 10 parliamentary fronts and 26 productive sector entities, project R$60–100 billion in new Brazilian investments over the next four years.

item.title: Governo lança programa de R$ 11 bilhões contra o crime organizado
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva launched the Brazil Against Organized Crime program, with a total investment of R$ 11 billion (R$ 1 billion from the Union Budget and R$ 10 billion via BNDES loans to states). The program, structured in four strategic axes — financial asphyxiation of criminal organizations, strengthening prison security, improving investigations and homicide clearance, and combating arms trafficking — aims to dismantle the economic, operational, and social bases of criminal gangs nationwide. State adherence is required to access BNDES funds, and the program will be formalized through a presidential decree and four ministerial ordinances.

item.title: Nunes Marques propôs regras de dupla checagem das urnas em 2026
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques, the new president of the TSE, strengthened in 2026 the double-checking rules for electronic ballots, allowing the first and last two voters of each polling section to accompany the issuance of the Zerésima and the closing of the Ballot Bulletin. This measure aims to increase transparency and trust in the electoral process, as voter oversight has existed since 2022 but was now detailed in TSE resolutions. The initiative comes amid disinformation about ballot integrity, following Bolsonaro’s convictions for abuse of political power and attempted coup in 2023 and 2025.

item.title: Nunes Marques deve adotar tom discreto no TSE nas eleições de 2026
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques of the STF is expected to adopt a more discreet tone as president of the TSE in the 2026 elections, favoring a less confrontational approach on issues such as disinformation and digital propaganda, while upholding the rules he helped draft. The anticipated shift suggests a more cautious stance in repressing political expressions, without breaking from the already-established resolutions.

item.title: Marcos Pontes vê risco de país tratar terras-raras como “nova soja”
item.description: Senator Marcos Pontes (PL-SP) warns that Brazil risks treating rare earths as a new soybean — exporting the raw material without adding value due to insufficient industrial and technological infrastructure for processing. He criticizes declining investments in science and technology, linking them to fiscal instability and misaligned priorities, and stresses that such investments are strategic and essential to reduce dependence on commodity exports. Pontes also states he supports Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential candidacy and is providing him with sector-related information.

item.title: Saiba quem é Nunes Marques, novo presidente do TSE
item.description: Kassio Nunes Marques assumed office as the new president of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) on May 12, 2026, succeeding Cármen Lúcia. He pledged a firmer stance against the irregular use of artificial intelligence in electoral campaigns. Appointed to the STF by Jair Bolsonaro in 2020, he previously played a notable role in electoral judgments involving the former president.

item.title: Nunes Marques assume TSE e comandará eleições
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques assumes the presidency of the TSE this Tuesday, replacing Cármen Lúcia, and will oversee the 2026 general elections, with André Mendonça as vice-president. Both were appointed to the STF by Jair Bolsonaro and have previously diverged from the Court’s majority. The ceremony will include Lula, the presidents of the Chamber and Senate, Flávio Bolsonaro, former presidents, and other officials.

item.title: PT vê risco no TSE, e Lula estreita laços com Nunes Marques
item.description: Lula attends the inauguration of Kassio Nunes Marques as the new president of the TSE, while the PT expresses concern over the Court’s new composition, fearing weakened efforts against disinformation following the departures of Alexandre de Moraes and Cármen Lúcia. Lula is cultivating a relationship with Nunes Marques through intermediaries Wellington Dias and Jorge Messias to ease institutional tensions in an election year.

item.title: Tarcísio intensifica viagens por SP e acelera repasses para reconstruir relação com prefeitos
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas has intensified municipal visits and accelerated fund disbursements to rebuild relationships with mayors after a period of strain. In April, he visited 17 cities in 15 days — 88% more than in the same period last year — and launched initiatives like the 3D Caravans and 'São Paulo pra Toda Obra', announcing R$ 2 billion for municipal improvements. The strategy aims to meet local demands before electoral restrictions take effect, with the government claiming continuous dialogue and having already disbursed over R$ 3.4 billion in agreements since the start of his term.

item.title: Em 200 dias, nenhum partido pediu ao TSE para fiscalizar urnas
item.description: In 200 days ahead of the 2026 elections, no political party has requested the TSE to inspect the electronic voting machines' source code, despite all parties being informed of the opportunity in October last year. The TSE allows source code inspection until shortly before the vote, a measure introduced in 2021 during Bolsonaro's government, who made unfounded attacks on the system. In 2023, the PL registered to inspect the source code for municipal elections but withdrew after attending a briefing at the Court.

item.title: Ex-presidente do BRB está na mesma cela que abrigou Bolsonaro
item.description: Former president of the Bank of Brasília (BRB), Paulo Henrique Costa, was transferred last Friday (9) to the 19th Military Police Battalion of the Federal District, known as 'Papudinha', where former President Jair Bolsonaro was previously held. The move was authorized by Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça. The article is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Lula reduz 10% da Lei Rouanet de incentivo fiscal à cultura
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed Complementary Law No. 224/2025, which establishes a linear 10% reduction in various federal tax benefits, including the Rouanet Law for cultural incentives, as part of a fiscal adjustment effort to improve government accounts. The measure, framed as necessary for fiscal responsibility, will affect culturally funded projects relying on tax renunciation, sparking debate among civil society groups and cultural policy experts. The full article is available only to subscribers.

item.title: Nunes Marques chega à presidência do TSE com bandeira de defesa da urna eletrônica, contrariando bolsonaristas
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques assumes the presidency of the TSE defending the electronic voting machine as a cornerstone of his term, contrary to expectations of Bolsonaro’s allies. He aims to strengthen trust in the electoral system through transparency, public verification of ballot issuance, dialogue with regional electoral courts, and cybersecurity measures. His agenda also includes countering the improper use of AI in campaigns, focusing on deepfake regulation and technical forensic partnerships.

item.title: Zeca Dirceu erra e publica foto da revista “Time” com Lula em 2022
item.description: Federal deputy Zeca Dirceu (PT-PR) shared on his X profile a photo of Time magazine's cover featuring Lula, claiming it was from this week's edition, although the cover was actually published on May 23, 2022, before the last presidential election. In the post, he cited praises from Barack Obama and Donald Trump about Lula, and the post was later corrected with a note indicating the actual date of the cover. The article also mentions a statement by Zeca Dirceu about Bolsonarists following an event with 130 people.

item.title: Crédito para taxistas e motoristas de app: veja as condições especiais que o governo planeja para as categorias
item.description: The government is preparing a subsidized credit line for taxi and app-based drivers, with interest rates around 12% per year — below the Selic rate of 14.5% and market rates above 20% — featuring a six-month grace period, up to six years for repayment, and a vehicle price cap of R$150,000. The program, expected to last four months as a provisional measure, is under debate over whether to restrict financing to sustainable vehicles (hybrids and electric) or allow all vehicles within the price limit, and will be submitted to President Lula for final approval.

item.title: Dino deve aguardar julgamento de recursos no TSE para destravar ação sobre eleições do Rio no STF
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino stated he will only allow the judgment of the action discussing the election model for Rio de Janeiro's government after the definitive ruling on pending clarification appeals at the TSE. He believes the Electoral Court's analysis is necessary to avoid conflicting decisions between the courts, as the case concerns the method for choosing a new governor following the incumbent's departure, with a legal dispute over direct versus indirect elections.

item.title: Às vésperas da eleição, pacote de Lula mira crime organizado, principal temor no país
item.description: The Lula government will launch an R$ 11 billion package to combat organized crime, with R$ 1 billion from the federal budget and R$ 10 billion in BNDES loans to states, targeting factions like PCC and CV. The initiative aims to improve public perception of security and counter U.S. pressure to label criminal groups as terrorists. Its success depends on voluntary state participation in accessing federal funds for national security and penitentiary funds.

item.title: Oposição entra com novo pedido de impeachment contra Moraes
item.description: The opposition bloc in the Chamber of Deputies filed a new impeachment request against Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, related to his suspension of the Dosimetry Law for those involved in the January 8 attacks. The PL party, led by Bolsonaro, claims over 42 Senate signatures support the move, but Senate President Davi Alcolumbre has not yet acted. Despite 102 impeachment requests against STF ministers since January 2021, none have ever been approved.

item.title: Nunes Marques toma posse como presidente do TSE em cerimônia com 1,5 mil convidados
item.description: Minister Kássio Nunes Marques was sworn in as president of the TSE in a ceremony with 1,500 guests, including President Lula and former presidents such as Bolsonaro, Dilma Rousseff, and José Sarney. He emphasized that the main challenge of his tenure will be combating the irregular use of artificial intelligence in the 2026 elections, particularly coordinated disinformation, deepfakes, and the simulation of real users on social media.

item.title: Puteiro aquático: famosa boate de luxo em Brasília fica alagada
item.description: The Paradise nightclub in Brasília's Hoteleiro Sul Sector was flooded due to burst pipes, turning its red velvet lounge into an aquatic emergency zone. The incident occurred on Mother's Day morning (May 12) and coincided with the city's preparations to host the 27th Mayors' March from May 18–21, raising concerns for owners Fayed and Louis Traboulsi, known for controlling gambling and nightlife in the DF.

item.title: A guerra política em torno da dosimetria dos atos golpistas - O Assunto #1717
item.description: Congress overturned President Lula's veto on the Dosimetry Law, which reduces sentences for those convicted of the January 8 attacks, but Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended its application pending constitutional review. Meanwhile, Bolsonarist lawmakers are pushing to revive the Amnesty PEC, proposing broad pardon for those involved in the coup attempt, heightening political tensions between the government and opposition.

item.title: IA será um dos maiores desafios de Nunes Marques no comando do TSE
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques assumes the presidency of the TSE with the mission of ensuring legality in the 2026 electoral campaign. Although the context is less turbulent than in 2022, with no evidence of a coup plot, he faces challenges such as AI-driven disinformation, persistent attacks on electronic voting machines, and heightened polarization, which increase the risk of electoral manipulation.

item.title: Estratégia global pesa na eleição nacional
item.description: Leading Brazilian presidential candidates for 2026 are already traveling internationally before the official electoral period begins, signaling a global strategy that influences the domestic race. Lula met with Donald Trump at the White House, while Flávio Bolsonaro visited El Salvador, Israel, France, Bahrain, and the United States (at least three times). Ronaldo Caiado and Tarcísio de Freitas were in Israel in 2024, and Romeu Zema traveled to San Salvador on a public security mission.

item.title: Democracia precisa se defender
item.description: The article argues that Brazilian democracy must be defended against the infiltration of organized crime into electoral processes, stating that the right to vote and run for office cannot serve as a shield for illegal activities. It emphasizes that safeguarding freedom of choice requires preventing marginal organizations from using elections to gain power through unlawful means.

item.title: Escala 6x1: Após unificação de propostas, ministros serão ouvidos pela comissão que analisa o assunto
item.description: The special committee in the Chamber analyzing workweek reduction will enter its second week with the presence of Lula government ministers and the engagement of Chamber President Hugo Motta. Finance Minister Dario Durigan will testify on Tuesday (12) on economic aspects, while General Secretariat Minister Guilherme Boulos will appear on Wednesday (13) to discuss social aspects and social dialogue. The strategy of holding daily sessions aims to speed up the PEC vote in the committee by May 26 and in the plenary on May 27, leveraging Motta’s support and government coordination to advance the proposal, a stated priority of Lula for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Governo federal lança plano de combate ao crime organizado; veja ações
item.description: The federal government launched the 'Brazil Against Organized Crime' program, focusing on financial suffocation of crime, prison security reinforcement, increased homicide clearance rates, and combating arms trafficking. The plan allocates R$11 billion, with R$1 billion from the 2026 budget and R$10 billion via BNDES loans to states, contingent on state adherence.

item.title: Lula tenta usar programa de segurança pública como trunfo eleitoral e mira em facções criminosas
item.description: The Lula government will launch the 'Brazil Against Organized Crime' program as an electoral trump card for 2026, focusing on isolating criminal faction leaders in 138 prisons using drones, cell phone blockers, and body scanners. The initiative, involving nearly R$1 billion in direct investment and R$10 billion in FIS/BNDES loans, also targets money laundering, aims to standardize homicide clearance rates nationwide, and seeks to curb arms trafficking through coordinated security force actions.

item.title: Posse de Nunes Marques na presidência do TSE terá jantar com ingresso a R$ 800
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques will take office as president of the TSE this Friday (12) and host a dinner with tickets priced at R$ 800, organized by Ajufe under an adhesion model. The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled for 7 PM, followed by the dinner at 8:30 PM in Brasília’s Asa Sul. All former Brazilian presidents were invited, including Jair Bolsonaro and Fernando Collor, who are under house arrest and would require authorization from Minister Alexandre de Moraes to attend.

item.title: Nunes Marques toma posse como presidente do TSE nesta terça; André Mendonça assume a vice-presidência
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques will take office as president of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) on Tuesday (12), succeeding Minister Cármen Lúcia. He will lead the Electoral Court in the October 2026 elections, which will determine the new president, senators, deputies, and governors. Minister André Mendonça will assume the vice-presidency of the TSE in the same ceremony.

item.title: É muita ignorância beber detergente contaminado, diz Janja
item.description: First Lady Janja and Health Minister Alexandre Padilha condemned the spread of misinformation regarding Anvisa, after Bolsonaro supporters ingested contaminated Ypê detergent in protest. Janja called the behavior 'utter ignorance' during a COVID-19 victims' memorial, while Padilha emphasized the health agency's decision was technically based and noted its director was appointed under Bolsonaro's government.

item.title: Renan Santos critica “histeria” da direita no caso Ypê
item.description: Renan Santos, a pré-candidate for Presidency from Missão, criticized the right-wing reaction to Anvisa's ban on Ypê detergent production, calling it 'hysteria' and accusing Bolsonaro supporters of politicizing the decision without evidence. He cited examples such as people drinking detergent as online protest and criticized Bolsonarist lawmakers for focusing on trivial issues like Havaianas advertisements or laws to force Neymar to play in the World Cup, rather than substantive policies.

item.title: Em discursos como deputado, Flávio deixou de lado saúde e educação para defender polícia
item.description: During his 16 years as a state deputy in Rio de Janeiro, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) focused his speeches on salary raises, pensions, workforce expansion, and benefits for security forces, sidelining issues such as health and education.
